headline_marked: State Minister [[Ishraque announces resignation]] to focus on anti-drug drive
headline: State Minister Ishraque announces resignation to focus on anti-drug drive
summary: Ishraque stated he voluntarily stepped down to avoid embarrassing his party and to dedicate himself to fighting narcotics.
details: State Minister Ishraque has announced his resignation from the ministry, stating that he is doing so voluntarily.
During a press conference at the National Press Club, he clarified that his party did not want him to resign, but he chose to do so on his own.
Ishraque explained that his decision was aimed at ensuring the party is not embarrassed and to allow him to focus more effectively on anti-drug operations.
He declared that his commitment to the fight against narcotics will continue even after leaving his ministerial position.
Addressing other queries, he also mentioned his readiness for the mayoral election if the party desires his candidacy.
caption:
State Minister Ishraque has voluntarily resigned from his post. He says he's doing it to protect his party and lead a war on drugs.

State Minister Ishraque has announced his resignation from the ministry, stating that he is doing so voluntarily.

During a press conference at the National Press Club, he clarified that his party did not want him to resign, but he chose to do so on his own.

Ishraque explained that his decision was aimed at ensuring the party is not embarrassed and to allow him to focus more effectively on anti-drug operations.

He declared that his commitment to the fight against narcotics will continue even after leaving his ministerial position.

Addressing other queries, he also mentioned his readiness for the mayoral election if the party desires his candidacy.

#Bangladesh #Politics #Resignation #AntiDrug #Dhaka

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV, The Daily Star, bdnews24.com

headline_marked: [[Two Bangladeshis executed in Saudi Arabia]], MoFA calls it disappointing
headline: Two Bangladeshis executed in Saudi Arabia, MoFA calls it disappointing
summary: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir says there were lapses in diplomatic communication and information exchange regarding the executions.
details: Two Bangladeshi citizens were executed in Saudi Arabia on charges of 'immoral acts' in the Masjid area of Makkah, according to reports from Middle Eastern media.
caption:
Two Bangladeshis have been executed in Saudi Arabia. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs says there were 'lapses' in diplomatic communication.

Two Bangladeshi citizens were executed in Saudi Arabia on charges of 'immoral acts' in the Masjid area of Makkah, according to reports from Middle Eastern media.
